objectives: This systematic review and meta-analysis examined the association between digital biomarkers of health obtained from wrist-worn wearables and anxiety in adults.
inclusion_criteria: This systematic review focused on anxiety, both clinical anxiety and anxiety symptoms. Using the PECOS framework, studies were selected if they (1) involved adults with a mean age of >18 years; (2) reported data from research- or consumer-grade wrist-worn devices; (3) did not require a control group, although studies including participants without anxiety were considered as comparators when applicable; (4) assessed generalized anxiety disorder or anxiety symptoms using standardized assessments (eg, self-report questionnaires or clinical diagnoses); and (5) used cross-sectional or longitudinal designs. Studies published in an English-language, peer-reviewed journal or thesis/dissertation, and studies that examined the relationship between anxiety and digital biomarkers via inferential statistics or machine learning methods were also eligible.
exclusion_criteria: Studies were excluded if they (1) focused on a sample that received diagnoses of neurodegenerative disorders or physical health conditions, although studies were eligible if participants without these conditions were analyzed separately; and (2) primarily focused on participants with a psychiatric comorbidity, neurological disorder, or stroke (>50% of the sample).
pmid_query: The review searched Medline, Embase, PsycINFO, Web of Science, CINAHL, and ProQuest Dissertations & Theses Global, supplemented by the first 300 Google Scholar records and reference-list screening. Multimedia Appendix 4 states that the core Medline strategy combined the digital-biomarker string "(wearable* or \"digital biomarker*\" or smartwatch* or \"smart watch\" or \"apple watch\" or applewatch or fitbit or Samsung or garmin or lg or Huawei or sony or xiaomi or adidas or nike or axivity or pedometer* or \"fitness track*\" or \"fitness monitor*\" or acceleromet* or \"activity monitor*\" or \"activity track*\" or actigraphy).ti,ab,kw" with the psychosocial-risk-factor string "(depress* or anxiet* or anxious* or \"post-traumatic stress disorder\" or PTSD or lonel* or \"social isolation\" or psychosis or psychotic or schizophreni* or bipolar).ti,ab,kw" using AND; the manuscript also states that the final update on September 21, 2025 restricted the second concept to anxiety-related terms.
selection_evidence: Results report 44 studies from 42 articles total: 36 studies from 35 inferential-statistics articles and 8 studies from 7 machine-learning articles. Table 1 explicitly labels the 35 inferential-study articles as refs 35-69, and Table 2 labels the 7 machine-learning articles as refs 70-76, yielding 42 included articles overall. The manuscript also notes that only a subset of cross-sectional sleep studies was quantitatively pooled, but Tables 1-2 enumerate the full included-study article set for this review/meta-analysis paper.
notes:
Cross-checking the reference list found likely internal citation inconsistencies in the manuscript: Table 1 labels the family-caregiver Ahn study as [35], but the matching citation appears later as ref 77 in the reference list and is also cited as [77] in the sleep-efficiency narrative; Table 1 entry "Uchida and Kurosawa, 2025 [55]" also does not cleanly match reference 55 in the reference list. Because the manuscript itself explicitly numbers the included-study set as 35-76 in Tables 1-2 and that numbering matches the reported total of 42 included articles, those exact table numbers are returned here.

Manual update note: Manual review confirmed row 38 has no PMID and the other remaining unresolved studies are not indexed in PubMed; gold_pmids reflect only OK rows.
pmid_query_exact_source: (wearable*[Title/Abstract] OR "digital biomarker*"[Title/Abstract] OR smartwatch*[Title/Abstract] OR "smart watch"[Title/Abstract] OR "apple watch"[Title/Abstract] OR applewatch[Title/Abstract] OR fitbit[Title/Abstract] OR Samsung[Title/Abstract] OR garmin[Title/Abstract] OR lg[Title/Abstract] OR Huawei[Title/Abstract] OR sony[Title/Abstract] OR xiaomi[Title/Abstract] OR adidas[Title/Abstract] OR nike[Title/Abstract] OR axivity[Title/Abstract] OR pedometer*[Title/Abstract] OR "fitness track*"[Title/Abstract] OR "fitness monitor*"[Title/Abstract] OR acceleromet*[Title/Abstract] OR "activity monitor*"[Title/Abstract] OR "activity track*"[Title/Abstract] OR actigraphy[Title/Abstract]) AND (anxiet*[Title/Abstract] OR anxious*[Title/Abstract])
pmid_query_repair_notes: Original pmid_query used Ovid/Medline .ti,ab,kw syntax which is not executable in PubMed. Source strategy recovered from supp_4.txt (Multimedia Appendix 4 overview of search terms). Converted .ti,ab,kw to [Title/Abstract] field tags. Second concept restricted to anxiety-related terms per manuscript statement that final update on September 21, 2025 restricted second concept to anxiety terms.
